title: "IPUMS_Clean"
output: html_document

```{r Step 1 Cleaning IPUMS Data, include=TRUE}
# ============================================================
# CPS ASEC CLEANING
# Wage Premium / Good Jobs Measure
#
# Project: Precariat Politics
#
# Purpose:
#   Clean the IPUMS-CPS ASEC extract and construct the
#   baseline analytic sample for estimating an industry-level
#   wage premium.
#
# Source:
#   IPUMS-CPS ASEC
#
# Years:
#   2000-2024
#
# IMPORTANT:
#   This script cleans and constructs the analytic sample.
#   The wage-premium model is estimated separately.
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Setup
# ------------------------------------------------------------

library(tidyverse)
library(here)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Load raw IPUMS extract
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_wage_clean <- read_csv(
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "IPUMS_CPS",
    "cps_wage_analysis_2000_2024.csv"
  )
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Clean IPUMS special values
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# IPUMS uses special numeric values for NIU, unknown,
# refused, and other non-substantive responses.
#
# For this analysis, the major variables requiring explicit
# treatment are:
#
#   wage_income
#   usual_hours_last_year
#   weeks_worked
#   industry
#   occupation
#   education
#   employment status
#   class of worker
#
# We retain the original variables and create cleaned versions
# rather than modifying the raw values in place.


cps_wage_clean <- cps_wage %>%

  mutate(

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Earnings
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    wage_income_clean = case_when(
      wage_income >= 0 &
        wage_income < 99999999 ~ wage_income,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Usual weekly hours
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    usual_hours_clean = case_when(
      usual_hours_last_year >= 1 &
        usual_hours_last_year <= 99 ~
        usual_hours_last_year,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Weeks worked
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    weeks_worked_clean = case_when(
      weeks_worked >= 0 &
        weeks_worked <= 52 ~
        weeks_worked,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Industry
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    industry_clean = case_when(
      industry > 0 ~ industry,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Occupation
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    occupation_clean = case_when(
      occupation > 0 ~ occupation,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ),

    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # ASEC weight
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    asecwt_clean = case_when(
      asecwt > 0 ~ asecwt,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )

  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Education
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# EDUC is harmonized by IPUMS across years.
#
# We preserve the original EDUC variable and create a
# simplified education category.
#
# The exact category definitions will be retained through
# the IPUMS-labelled original variable.

cps_wage_clean <- cps_wage_clean %>%

  mutate(

    educ_category = case_when(

      educ == 1 ~ "No schooling",

      educ == 2 ~ "Less than 1st grade",

      educ == 10 ~ "1st, 2nd, 3rd, or 4th grade",

      educ == 20 ~ "5th or 6th grade",

      educ == 30 ~ "7th or 8th grade",

      educ == 40 ~ "9th grade",

      educ == 50 ~ "10th grade",

      educ == 60 ~ "11th grade",

      educ == 71 ~ "12th grade, no diploma",

      educ == 73 ~ "High school graduate",

      educ == 81 ~ "Some college, no degree",

      educ == 91 ~ "Associate degree, occupational",

      educ == 92 ~ "Associate degree, academic",

      educ == 111 ~ "Bachelor's degree",

      educ == 123 ~ "Master's degree",

      educ == 124 ~ "Professional degree",

      educ == 125 ~ "Doctorate",

      TRUE ~ NA_character_

    )

  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Approximate years of schooling
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# This is an analytic approximation rather than a replacement
# for the original IPUMS EDUC variable.
#
# We retain EDUC because the categorical measure can be used
# in the final wage equation if preferred.

cps_wage_clean <- cps_wage_clean %>%

  mutate(

    years_schooling = case_when(

      educ == 1   ~ 0,
      educ == 2   ~ 0,
      educ == 10  ~ 2,
      educ == 20  ~ 5,
      educ == 30  ~ 7,
      educ == 40  ~ 9,
      educ == 50  ~ 10,
      educ == 60  ~ 11,
      educ == 71  ~ 12,
      educ == 73  ~ 12,
      educ == 81  ~ 14,
      educ %in% c(91, 92) ~ 14,
      educ == 111 ~ 16,
      educ == 123 ~ 18,
      educ == 124 ~ 19,
      educ == 125 ~ 20,

      TRUE ~ NA_real_

    )

  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Potential labor-market experience
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Standard Mincer-style approximation:
#
# potential experience =
#   age - years of schooling - 6
#
# Negative values are set to missing.

cps_wage_clean <- cps_wage_clean %>%

  mutate(

    potential_experience =
      age - years_schooling - 6,

    potential_experience =
      if_else(
        potential_experience >= 0,
        potential_experience,
        NA_real_
      ),

    potential_experience_sq =
      potential_experience^2

  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Baseline worker sample
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Conceptual baseline:
#
#   Age 25-64
#   Positive wage income
#   At least some weeks worked
#   Full-time based on usual weekly hours
#   Valid industry
#   Valid occupation
#   Valid survey weight
#
# We deliberately DO NOT impose 50+ weeks at this stage.
# Annual work intensity will be retained for robustness checks.


cps_wage_analysis <- cps_wage_clean %>%

  filter(

    # Prime-age workers
    age >= 25,
    age <= 64,

    # Positive annual wage/salary income
    wage_income_clean > 0,

    # Worked during the year
    weeks_worked_clean > 0,

    # Full-time
    usual_hours_clean >= 35,

    # Valid industry and occupation
    !is.na(industry_clean),
    !is.na(occupation_clean),

    # Valid survey weight
    !is.na(asecwt_clean),

    # Valid education / experience
    !is.na(years_schooling),
    !is.na(potential_experience)

  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 8. Construct log earnings
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_wage_analysis <- cps_wage_analysis %>%

  mutate(

    log_wage_income =
      log(wage_income_clean)

  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 9. Create alternative annual-work measures
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# These will allow us to examine whether the estimated
# industry premium depends on the annual work threshold.

cps_wage_analysis <- cps_wage_analysis %>%

  mutate(

    worked_26plus_weeks =
      weeks_worked_clean >= 26,

    worked_40plus_weeks =
      weeks_worked_clean >= 40,

    worked_50plus_weeks =
      weeks_worked_clean >= 50,

    full_year_worker =
      weeks_worked_clean >= 50

  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 10. Create baseline full-year robustness sample
# ------------------------------------------------------------

cps_wage_full_year <- cps_wage_analysis %>%

  filter(
    weeks_worked_clean >= 50
  )


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 11. Create descriptive sample statistics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

sample_statistics <- cps_wage_analysis %>%

  summarise(

    observations = n(),

    years = n_distinct(year),

    mean_age = mean(
      age,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    mean_wage =
      weighted.mean(
        wage_income_clean,
        asecwt_clean,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    median_wage =
      median(
        wage_income_clean,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    mean_hours =
      weighted.mean(
        usual_hours_clean,
        asecwt_clean,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    mean_weeks =
      weighted.mean(
        weeks_worked_clean,
        asecwt_clean,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )

  )


print(sample_statistics)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 12. Annual sample sizes
# ------------------------------------------------------------

annual_sample <- cps_wage_analysis %>%

  group_by(year) %>%

  summarise(

    n = n(),

    weighted_n =
      sum(
        asecwt_clean,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    mean_wage =
      weighted.mean(
        wage_income_clean,
        asecwt_clean,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    mean_hours =
      weighted.mean(
        usual_hours_clean,
        asecwt_clean,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    mean_weeks =
      weighted.mean(
        weeks_worked_clean,
        asecwt_clean,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"

  )


write_csv(
  annual_sample,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "IPUMS_CPS",
    "CPS_WagePremium_AnnualSample.csv"
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 13. Industry-year sample sizes
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_sample <- cps_wage_analysis %>%

  group_by(
    year,
    industry_clean
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    n = n(),

    weighted_n =
      sum(
        asecwt_clean,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"

  )


write_csv(
  industry_sample,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "IPUMS_CPS",
    "CPS_WagePremium_IndustrySample.csv"
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 14. Industry-year descriptive earnings
# ------------------------------------------------------------

industry_wages <- cps_wage_analysis %>%

  group_by(
    year,
    industry_clean
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    n = n(),

    weighted_mean_wage =
      weighted.mean(
        wage_income_clean,
        asecwt_clean,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    weighted_mean_log_wage =
      weighted.mean(
        log_wage_income,
        asecwt_clean,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

    .groups = "drop"

  )


write_csv(
  industry_wages,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "IPUMS_CPS",
    "CPS_WagePremium_IndustryWages.csv"
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 15. Save cleaned baseline sample
# ------------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(
  cps_wage_analysis,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "IPUMS_CPS",
    "cps_wage_analysis_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 16. Save full-year robustness sample
# ------------------------------------------------------------

saveRDS(
  cps_wage_full_year,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "IPUMS_CPS",
    "cps_wage_full_year_2000_2024.rds"
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 17. Save CSV
# ------------------------------------------------------------

write_csv(
  cps_wage_analysis,
  here(
    "01_tidydata",
    "IPUMS_CPS",
    "cps_wage_analysis_2000_2024.csv"
  )
)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# END
# ------------------------------------------------------------
```
